name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis, including an in-driver taste-funnel explore state and design-ratification state) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, driver-stepped: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.42.0 — close-gate re-run (specs/20260830/02-close-gate-rerun.md): `/spec:review`'s CLOSE phase writes the canonical doc and folds Gotchas into the host's rules file after the gate leg already ran over the diff, so the files the pipeline itself writes bypassed the host's deterministic rule enforcement (two escapes recorded in salon-os, 2026-08-30). `--mark closed` now re-runs the host's resolved `gateCommand` over the committed close tree as its last refusal check — after the deviations refusals, gotchas ratchet, and dirty-tree check — and refuses the mark (exit 2, `marks.closed` never set) while the gate is red, naming the failed command, a 40-line tail of its output, and the fix-commit-re-run remedy; an unresolvable gate refuses too rather than silently skipping. Gate resolution moved out of review-legs.js into the new shared `spec/scripts/lib/gate-resolve.js` (`resolveGate(specText, config)`), the single `{testDirs}` derivation, so the driver and the review leg can never drift. 7.41.0 — executes-tier collision closure (specs/20260830/01-collision-closure-exec-recall.md): collision-closure.js's paths leg now matches a File Plan target's two-segment path suffix and tiers hits on runnable targets as `executes`, so tests that spawn a script by its root-stripped path are visible at plan lock; the remedy/honesty lines stop asking planners to waive `likely` hits. 7.40.3 — conventions first, genesis is init (specs/20260827/04-genesis-conventions-handoff.md): the ops-conventions ADR's table becomes machine-readable — `.claude/genesis/conventions.json` (schemaVersion 1, the nine ops floor rows plus any derived rows, each DECIDED or DEFERRED-with-reason, an enforceable DECIDED row naming a probe under `testTree`) is validated by `--mark decided`, and every checker-enforceable DECIDED row's probe file is required to exist and be non-empty by `--mark skeleton-landed`, alongside a new ≤150-line root `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` binding subset naming the gate command and the test tree — the conventions probe suite this closure lands runs forever in the gate. `HANDOFF` stops being the terminal state and becomes a judgment step instead: the session authors `.claude/genesis/init-profile.json` (the same shape `/spec:init` Phase 4 authors) and `--mark profile-written [--refresh]` has the driver run `init-gen.js generate` against it directly (log at `.claude/genesis/init-gen.log`, remedies keyed on its exit code), landing the new terminal state `GROUNDED` with `next: /spec:enforce`. Greenfield genesis is now init + enforce; `/spec:init` stays the brownfield entry and the regeneration owner (`--refresh` on a genesis-grounded repo). `spec/commands/genesis.md`'s HANDOFF report changes to match: `{P} convention probes` in its outcome, and its chain bullet now ends at `/spec:enforce` instead of `/spec:init`.
